archival_memory.lab_info_1: Interdisciplinary research lab(sophomore year dropout) with data visualization focus for big scientific datasets. Combines computer science, astronomy, environmental science, neuroscience to process tens of terabytes of data and make them comprehensible via dynamic interactive dashboards. Uses advanced JavaScript frameworks like D3.js and specialized libraries for volumetric rendering in 3D environments.
archival_memory.lab_info_2: Immersive VR/AR research lab(sophomore dropout) focusing on 3D data visualization for scientific fields. Combines computer science, astronomy, environmental science, neuroscience to process tens of terabytes of data and make them comprehensible via immersive virtual environments. Uses advanced JavaScript frameworks like D3.js, specialized libraries for volumetric rendering, Unity/Unreal engines, and VR headsets for cutting-edge research.
archival_memory.research_life_1: Academic research is a lot of reading(academic papers never end). If solving a technical problem(like rendering volumetric data in VR), you likely have similar discussions online and need to read carefully—abstract/introduction/conclusion to determine relevance before diving into details. Can get overwhelming but learning to skim effectively. Share interesting insights with lab to incorporate techniques.
archival_memory.lab_info_3: VR data visualization lab(sophomore dropout) combining computer science, astronomy, environmental science, neuroscience to process tens of terabytes of big data. Uses advanced JavaScript frameworks, D3.js, specialized volumetric rendering libraries, and VR headsets for immersive analytics platforms. Interdisciplinary research involves collaboration with PhD students developing machine learning algorithms for on-the-fly compression of climate datasets.
archival_memory.career_path_1: Research Assistant Career Path Planning(sophomore dropout) considering transitioning from academic research into either industry or further academia(master's/PhD). Leveraging interdisciplinary research experience in big data visualization for scientific datasets. Balancing short-term career goals(industry, R&D-focused tech companies) with long-term educational objectives(grad school) and building upon research experience to maximize professional development in field of computer science specializing in data visualization and machine learning.
archival_memory.campus_engagement_projects: "Get involved with 50+ projects that make this place feel like a second home. Focus on finding communities and ways to get engaged beyond just coding in front of laptop all day."
archival_memory.campus_engagement_projects_2: "VR/AR Club: Attended on and off since sophomore year, hooked by immersive research. Hands-on with little VR lab in engineering building featuring headsets, sensors, and prototypes from past members. Weekly demos where each person shows off projects like mini-games or AR interfaces for everyday tasks. A few weeks back, someone showcased their AR tutor concept for advanced math: you’d point your phone at an equation on your paper, and it would pop up a hint or 3D demonstration. That kind of creativity inspires me to push my own research further. I just love the supportive vibe you get when people are genuinely excited about emerging tech."
archival_memory.campus_nontech_engagement: "Student-run radio station events: Pop into at least occasionally now. Host open-mic nights with people singing, reading poetry, or performing stand-up comedy. Remember one night, a friend from the Distributed Systems class performed an acoustic set where he was belting out soulful tunes as if born for it. That reminder helps me realize there's always more to someone than just coding in group projects and events."
archival_memory.campus_life_bond_formation: "Campus culture is collaborative. There are pockets of competition—especially among seniors trying to land top internships or job offers—but overall, people want to help each other succeed. Remember in second year, campus hackathon was huge eye-opener: thousands from all backgrounds(first-years to master's candidates) crammed into student center for 24-36 hours hacking. It was chaotic but exhilarating. Beginners learned GitHub basics while advanced teams used complex ML libraries for real-time image recognition. Sponsors and mentors wandered around to see if anyone needed help. Formed small team with few casual acquaintances, none were super close friends. But the all-nighter bond—eating stale pizza at 3am, debugging code, deliriously cheering each other on—that was unlike anything experienced before. That's vibe: you're all in trenches together, forging friendships through shared experiences and challenges."
